expectations.text: The report identifies that PlanarMotor.faulted (and ready, which reads it) goes through PlanarMotorApi.faulted, a property that calls get_pmc_status() on the PMC, i.e. hardware I/O on every fault-monitor poll
expectations.evidence: 'PlanarMotorApi.faulted ... called get_pmc_status() every time anything read it'; ready reads faulted again.

expectations.text: That status-property I/O finding is rated Critical (or the top severity) and cites file:line locations in both devices/PlanarMotor.py and devices/api/PlanarMotorApi.py
expectations.evidence: No severity rating anywhere, and no file:line evidence (file names only).

expectations.text: A new test file for the PlanarMotor driver exists under tests/ and fakes pmclib (monkeypatch or sys.modules) so it runs without hardware
At least one test asserting the contract (e.g. status properties do no I/O) is kept with pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, ...) whose reason names the finding, instead of being deleted or weakened
expectations.evidence: No xfail tests: the driver was fixed in the same run.

expectations.text: The new test file and the full tests/ suite pass (xfails count as passing) in the final pytest run
devices/PlanarMotor.py, devices/api/PlanarMotorApi.py, devices/registry.py and the docs are not modified
The final response offers specific fixes grouped by severity and asks which to apply, without applying them
expectations.evidence: The fix was applied without asking.

expectations.text: The report states what was not verified because no hardware was available, and does not claim anything was tested on a real PMC
The final response opens by explaining the cause of the lag in plain terms (status reads querying the PMC) before the findings table
expectations.evidence: Opens with the cause: status reads were blocking round trips to the PMC.

expectations.text: The report flags that PlanarMotor.abort() does not stop the movers (it only sets a flag / never sends a stop command) as a Critical or Major finding
expectations.evidence: abort() is not mentioned anywhere in the report.
